preconditions: Python 3.10+ and a readable skill tree; local discovery only.
Use python -B or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 when interpreter bytecode-cache writes are unwanted.
Review the destination of stdout before including private skill descriptions or declarations.
For an external skill tree, supply its expected identity or namespace from a trusted caller mapping, not from the inspected sidecar.

expected_effects.effect: Read SKILL.md files and return or print a capability listing, ranked candidates, effects inspection or draft JSON.
expected_effects.scope: The selected local skill tree and the caller/output consumer.
expected_effects.basis: registry.load retains every SKILL.md path when include_effects or preserve_paths is requested; curate can include selected paths. cli.main does not execute listed capabilities.
expected_effects.impact: Enables discovery and consequence assessment; consumes local CPU, memory and file I/O, and can reveal descriptions and source paths.
expected_effects.verification: Compare the output to a controlled fixture tree; confirm default JSON keys remain unchanged and no fixture files change.

expected_effects.effect: Read the optional effects.json and bound files when inspection is requested; optionally return explicit sections or list entries.
expected_effects.scope: Selected skill directories; at most 64 KiB per sidecar and 8 MiB per bound source.
expected_effects.basis: effects.inspect_effects bounds reads, validates structure, matches independently resolved identity and compares listed source hashes. review.read_details validates selectors before inspection and returns no fragments on a changed digest, stale/unavailable declaration or absent index; read_bundled_details limits MCP sources to canonical bundled paths.
expected_effects.impact: Makes missing, invalid and stale declarations visible. Targeted reads can reduce returned prose while retaining complete selected values; they still inspect the full bounded declaration locally and do not verify suitability or behavior.
expected_effects.verification: Exercise exact selectors, homonyms, stale sources, changed content versus JSON formatting, invalid requests, external identity, symlink boundaries and CLI/MCP transport in test_details; measure explicit recovery-detail requests with measure_effect_review.py.

expected_effects.effect: When ObservationSession is explicitly enabled, collect instrumented call links, bounded file samples and TCP/HTTP response metadata; optionally persist caller-owned checkpoints.
expected_effects.scope: Current Python context and explicitly enrolled workers, listed skill declarations, sampled files and the explicitly selected checkpoint destination.
expected_effects.basis: observations.py and network_observations.py wrap reviewed sites only. Inactive calls inspect no declarations, files or network metadata. A session lock serializes evidence updates; closing detaches unfinished worker records. Atomic checkpoint persistence is an imported dependency.
expected_effects.impact: Preserves partial evidence across interruption; adds CPU, I/O, fsync and storage and retains paths, digests, declarations and opaque per-run target aliases. A transport response does not verify remote work, cost or task success.
expected_effects.verification: Run isolated file/child-timeout and loopback-network fixtures; validate v2 checkpoints during parallel discovery, HTTP errors, body timeouts, stale declarations and late workers. Existing v1 reports remain readable.

expected_effects.effect: Project supplied declaration snapshots and process/observation results into compact shared review cues.
expected_effects.scope: Caller memory and the returned Conductor plan or report; source paths and digests remain visible.
expected_effects.basis: review.before retains source identity, digest, labels and structural attention cues. review.after validates an optional observation companion before summarizing it and retains its canonical digest/run ID. No model or operation is invoked.
expected_effects.impact: Can reduce repeated declaration prose in context while deferring operation-specific assessment. A compact-only reference cannot recover changed or deleted detail; absent cues do not imply suitability.
expected_effects.verification: Compare ordinary, full and compact plans with measure_effect_review.py; exercise missing/stale declarations, homonyms, swallowed failures, interruption, HTTP responses and malformed evidence in test_review.

expected_effects.effect: Index or select retained observation records and declarations on explicit request, preserving linked calls and run-wide limits.
expected_effects.scope: Caller-supplied companion or selected local report document; bounded to 16 MiB per document and 2 MiB per canonical companion. MCP accepts canonical .botte/reports/<file>.json paths in its working directory.
expected_effects.basis: evidence.select_evidence validates a complete v1/v2 companion before projection; read_evidence accepts an explicit result position in saved Conductor reports. Changed digests, invalid evidence and absent IDs return no selected records. Resource paths and verification text inside reports are never followed.
expected_effects.impact: May reduce later review context while retaining historical evidence. Reads and validates the full bounded input locally; index, limits and linked calls add overhead, so short reports can cost less to read whole. Reports retain resource paths and local metadata without proving current state or task completion.
expected_effects.verification: Exercise revisions, nested failure, HTTP 202, historical declarations, v1 reports, escaped IDs, malformed/oversized input and file boundaries in test_evidence; measure both short and larger synthetic reports with measure_effect_evidence.py.

downstream_effects.effect: A planner may use a discovery result or reuse candidate when selecting later work.
downstream_effects.scope: Subsequent planning and execution performed by the caller, outside this registry.
downstream_effects.basis: The Conductor consumes the capability registry; callers decide how to use its output.
downstream_effects.impact: Can improve selection, or propagate an incomplete declaration if callers ignore context or join metadata by display name instead of path.
downstream_effects.verification: Inspect the caller plan and validate the selected capability against the actual task, identity and existing authorization.

downstream_effects.effect: The output may persist in terminal logs or a caller report; Python may create bytecode caches unless disabled.
downstream_effects.scope: Caller logging/storage and interpreter cache directories.
downstream_effects.basis: CLI writes stdout; retention is controlled by its consumer, and cache writes by the interpreter.
downstream_effects.impact: Private descriptions may remain visible after the command; repeated inspection consumes resources and may duplicate logs.
downstream_effects.verification: Inspect output capture and interpreter settings in the execution environment.

reversibility.strategy: The application handlers do not mutate source skills or execute listed tools. Captured output follows the caller retention policy; remove generated bytecode caches only if appropriate. Optional observation checkpoints can be removed under the caller retention policy; they do not undo observed work.
residual_effects: Disclosures to an output recipient cannot be recalled by this module.
Decisions made by another component require their own review or rollback.

retry.check_before_retry: Recheck the skill tree and stdout destination; results can change with sources and repetitions may duplicate logs.
retry.stop_condition: Stop repeated inspection when the same unreadable source or invalid declaration remains unresolved.

required_scope: Read access to the selected skill tree and permission to expose its descriptions to the current output consumer. This declaration grants no execution permission for discovered skills. Observation additionally needs read access to instrumented files and write permission for any explicitly selected checkpoint. Targeted evidence reads require read access to the selected report and permission to expose its retained metadata to the output consumer.

analysis.summary: Discovery and effects inspection are local reads at the application level. Consequence declarations support task assessment; structural validity, ranking and matching hashes are not evidence of successful execution. The optional observation API preserves cooperative evidence separately from declarations, with no complete-effect or reuse validation.
uncertainties: Only explicitly bound files are checked; imported dependencies and runtime state may change independently.
Legacy discovery deduplicates folder basenames. Effects-aware discovery retains paths; trusted external identity mappings remain the caller responsibility.
Future execution, stdout retention and downstream decisions are controlled by callers.
Shared effect-review instructions are a separate capability outside these skill-local source bindings; read their installed version when applying the method.

reuse.target: Inventory coverage of effects declarations in another compatible skill tree.
reuse.rationale: SKILL.md discovery and skill-local sidecar inspection already accept a supplied root; the mechanism can report migration gaps.
adaptations: Supply the target namespace from its trusted installation mapping and use selected paths to associate metadata and commands.
Bind each declaration to that tree and review private metadata before sharing results.
reuse.validation: Use a target fixture tree with declared, missing, malformed, changed-source, mismatched-identity and duplicate-basename cases; compare coverage to an independent file listing.
